To address severe class imbalance, the authors describe implementing a CTGAN model with a generator and discriminator each having three fully-connected hidden layers of 256 neurons, trained for 300 epochs, and further augmented with SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE. CTGAN's conditional generation and mode-specific normalization concepts are adopted as the minority-class data augmentation mechanism underlying the whole training pipeline, described via a custom-built architecture rather than a cited library call.

The authors explicitly identify the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) as an open-source library offering CTGAN, CopulaGAN, Gaussian Copula, TVAE and Bayesian Networks, and use the CTGAN package (with tuned epochs/batch-size hyperparameters) to generate 10,000 synthetic procurement records used to train and test the classification pipeline. paper-transforming-wearable-personal-hea.summary: This paper introduces PHIA (Personal Health Insights Agent), an LLM agent that uses multistep reasoning with code generation and information retrieval to answer numerical and open-ended questions about wearable health data, evaluated with two large benchmark datasets and extensive human expert review. To build one benchmark, the authors synthesize 30,000 synthetic wearable users from real user data: a Gaussian Copula model captures correlations among static demographic attributes, and a Conditional Probabilistic Auto-Regressive (CPAR) model generates the sequential time-series data conditioned on those contexts. SDV's Gaussian Copula and CPAR sequential synthesizers are run directly to produce the synthetic wearable population underlying the objective-questions evaluation benchmark.

paper-driven-hybrid-framework-generating.summary: This IEEE PES General Meeting paper proposes a novel hybrid CTGAN-TVAE architecture for generating synthetic renewable energy generation data to support power system resource adequacy and planning studies where historical data is scarce. The authors modify the internal loss functions and encoder/decoder/generator/discriminator interactions to fuse TVAE's latent representation with CTGAN's conditional GAN mechanism for conditioning on time, and compare the resulting model against DoppleGANger on real solar power datasets. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE architectures are taken as the starting point and their internals are re-engineered into a new combined generative model.

paper-generated-fall-assessing-llms-2025.summary: This paper investigates whether large language models (text-to-motion and text-to-text) and a diffusion-based method can generate synthetic wearable accelerometer data to improve LSTM-based fall detection, comparing the realism and downstream utility of the generated data against real baseline datasets. It finds diffusion-based data aligns closest with real accelerometer distributions while LLM-generated data helps most in low-frequency settings. In its related-work discussion the authors describe a prior study (Liaquat et al.) that evaluated SDV's PAR sequential model, TGAN, and CTGAN for fall-related time-series generation, noting CTGAN-generated data improved performance but still lagged real data; SDV's PAR and CTGAN are only cited and discussed as prior art, not run by this paper's own experiments.

paper-can-synthetic-fair-private-2025.summary: This paper compares five synthetic data generators (CTGAN, DistilGPT2/GReaT, ADSGAN, PATEGAN, DECAF) and several fairness pre-processing algorithms on learning-analytics datasets, evaluating trade-offs between privacy, fairness, and utility. It finds DECAF best balances privacy and fairness but sacrifices utility, and that applying fairness pre-processing to synthetic rather than real data yields greater fairness gains. CTGAN is run as one of the five synthetic data generators evaluated, with its conditional generator and training-by-sampling mechanism described and its outputs measured for fairness, privacy, and downstream AUC-ROC.

paper-comparing-language-models-differen.summary: This paper evaluates large language models of varying scales on generating and reasoning over multi-step, multi-table security queries derived from realistic security log scenarios, using a proposed diffusion-based synthetic data pipeline to address data scarcity in the security domain. In its related work on synthetic tabular data generation, it cites CTGAN as an early GAN-based method that suffers from mode collapse and poor handling of categorical variables, contrasting it with newer diffusion-based approaches like TabDDPM. CTGAN is only mentioned in the related-work discussion and is never run in the paper's own diffusion-based pipeline.

paper-evaluating-use-synthetic-machine-2.summary: This paper addresses data scarcity in predicting the self-healing capacity of bacteria-driven self-healing concrete by generating synthetic data to augment a small literature-derived dataset of 38 samples, then training and comparing several ML models (including random forest) for prediction accuracy. The authors used SDV's Gaussian Copula synthesizer to expand the dataset tenfold to 350 synthetic samples under default parameters, and used SDMetrics to evaluate synthetic data quality via Quality Score and Column Pair Trends metrics. SDV's GaussianCopula synthesizer is run as the sole data generator underpinning the entire ML training pipeline, with SDMetrics used to validate the synthetic data's statistical fidelity.

paper-fairtabformer-mitigating-bias-synt.summary: This paper proposes FairTabFormer, a GPT-2-decoder-based transformer generative model for synthetic tabular network traffic data that incorporates a fairness-aware loss penalizing disparity in prediction distributions across sensitive protocol-type groups. It is evaluated on the CIC IoT23 intrusion detection dataset, measuring downstream XGBoost utility alongside Demographic Parity Ratio/Difference fairness metrics. CTGAN is run as one of three state-of-the-art baselines (alongside TabFairGAN and REaLTabFormer), with its accuracy, DPD, and DPR results reported in the comparison table, while the earlier Tabular GAN (TGAN) paper is cited only for background on GAN-based tabular synthesis.

paper-generating-unseen-diseases-patient.summary: This paper presents Onto-CGAN, a generative framework that combines disease ontology embeddings with a conditional GAN to synthesize patient data for diseases entirely absent from the training set, evaluated on acute myeloid leukemia patient records for distributional fidelity, correlation structure, and downstream classifier utility. Onto-CGAN is built directly on the CTGAN architecture, using its mode-specific normalization for numerical variables and its conditional GAN design as the backbone, augmented with ontology-derived disease embeddings, and is benchmarked head-to-head against vanilla CTGAN throughout the experiments. CTGAN's conditional generator and mode-specific normalization scheme are extended into a new ontology-conditioned model, with plain CTGAN also run as the main comparison baseline.

paper-how-good-your-synthetic-2025.summary: This paper presents SynthRO, a GUI dashboard for evaluating and benchmarking synthetic tabular health data across resemblance, utility, and privacy dimensions, with automated ranking to help users select suitable synthetic data generators. SDV is run as one of several generation methods used to produce the validation datasets, and is also listed in a comparison table of existing synthetic-data evaluation tools (SDGym/SDMetrics).

Validated on real retail data, it reports significant revenue, margin, and sales uplift for a target customer segment. CTGAN is run to generate synthetic sales/bundle data for new products, addressing cold-start problems as one of several AI components in the pipeline.

To address the difficulty of obtaining sufficient real manufacturing data, the authors use CTGAN to generate synthetic tabular data augmenting their small dataset, then compare several base learners, with an ElasticNet model showing the best improvement in R2 and MAE. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is run as the generator producing synthetic training data to expand the limited real dataset.

paper-soft-hoeffding-tree-transparent-20.summary: This paper proposes soft Hoeffding trees (SoHoT), a differentiable and transparent tree model for data streams that combines the extensibility of Hoeffding trees with the gradient-based adaptability of soft trees, evaluated on 20 data streams against standard and limited Hoeffding trees and soft trees. To build synthetic evaluation streams with injected concept drift, the authors use CTGAN to emulate a realistic data distribution and oversample a randomly selected class to create abrupt drifts. CTGAN is run as the generator producing part of the synthetic benchmark data streams used in the experiments.

CTGAN is used as the generator to produce the synthetic minority samples underlying the augmented training dataset.

paper-importance-being-discrete-measurin.summary: This paper presents a measurement study of discretization strategies for differentially private (DP) marginal generative models for synthetic tabular data, comparing uniform, quantile, k-means, and PrivTree discretizers across six DP marginal models. paper-evaluating-effect-curing-condition.summary: This paper investigates how curing conditions affect the glass transition temperature of a structural adhesive, using a generative modeling approach to expand a limited experimental dataset for analysis. The title indicates the authors applied a conditional tabular generative adversarial network to model and predict the relationship between curing parameters and glass transition behavior. CTGAN is used as the generative method underpinning the study's empirical results.
paper-evaluating-effect-curing-condition.needs: No full text or abstract obtained; cannot confirm whether the authors used the sdv-dev CTGAN package directly (api_user) or reimplemented it, nor the exact role (sole generator vs. one of several) or dataset scale/augmentation purpose.

paper-ncgan-calibrated-oversampling-tech.summary: This paper proposes NCGAN, a GAN-based oversampling method for fraud detection that adds a second discriminator to calibrate synthetic fraudulent samples away from resembling non-fraudulent data, improving precision and F1 score across logistic regression, LightGBM, and TabNet classifiers on a credit card fraud dataset. CTGAN is run as one of the oversampling baselines alongside SMOTE, with its synthetic data distributions and downstream classifier performance directly compared against NCGAN's. CTGAN is used as a comparison baseline generator throughout the empirical evaluation, not modified or extended.
paper-ncgan-calibrated-oversampling-tech.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentences available, so exact experimental setup and whether SDV's own CTGAN package (vs. a reimplementation) was used cannot be confirmed.

paper-synthetic-generation-combinatorial.summary: This paper introduces CT-VAE, a synthetic data generation method that combines Variational Autoencoders with Combinatorial Testing to systematically sample the VAE's latent space (rather than sampling it randomly), aiming to produce synthetic tabular data whose downstream machine-learning utility matches real data while protecting sensitive information. The authors evaluate CT-VAE against several state-of-the-art synthetic data generation approaches on multiple datasets. The work's metadata record shows it cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper (Patki et al. 2016), but no SDV-family term or discussion appears anywhere in the extracted full text provided, so the nature of the citation could not be confirmed.
paper-synthetic-generation-combinatorial.needs: Full text passages around any SDV mention were not recoverable; unclear whether SDV was used as a comparison baseline (matching the abstract's claim of outperforming 'several state-of-the-art synthetic data generation approaches') or cited only in the bibliography. Middle sections of the paper (methods/results) were not available in the provided evidence.

paper-fairness-privacy-pre-processing-20.summary: This paper proposes a combinatorial-optimization framework that debiases datasets containing binary or non-binary protected attributes by selecting a fairness-optimal subset via heuristics such as genetic algorithms, with an option to use synthetic data instead of real records to also preserve privacy. Experiments on the Adult, Bank, and COMPAS datasets show genetic algorithms most effectively reduce discrimination measures. For the synthetic-data setting, the authors generate data using a Gaussian copula model, citing the Synthetic Data Vault paper as its source.
paper-fairness-privacy-pre-processing-20.needs: Not explicit whether the SDV library package itself (vs. a standalone Gaussian copula implementation) was used to run the model; treated as api_user given the direct citation of the SDV paper for the generation method actually executed.

paper-robot-assisted-generation-minimal-.summary: This paper presents a proof-of-concept robotic system for generating annotated training data for 6D object pose estimation with minimal human interaction, aiming to reduce reliance on synthetic-data pipelines that suffer from domain gap and require expert knowledge. The work targets robot manipulation in operational environments rather than tabular data synthesis. The SDV paper (Patki et al. 2016) is cited, apparently in passing, with no indication in the available evidence that the SDV library or its algorithms were actually used or engaged with.

paper-stacked-generalization-model-enhan.summary: This paper develops a stacked generalization model combining a multilayer perceptron regressor, support vector regression, and a linear regressor to predict earthquake-induced soil liquefaction settlement, using Korean geotechnical survey data from the 2016 Pohang earthquake and validating against individual base models. The work is a civil/geotechnical engineering machine-learning study with no synthetic-data generation component of its own. TGAN is cited once in the introduction only to illustrate that tabular generative adversarial networks can generate discrete and continuous values, with no library run or method adopted.

paper-synthesis-testing-black-box-2022.summary: This paper presents AITEST, a framework for automated synthesis of test data to evaluate black-box ML/DL classification models on tabular data, using constraint-based generation combined with a model-agnostic path coverage criterion derived from a global explainability algorithm (TREPAN) to test properties like fairness and robustness. The metadata indicates the paper cites the CTGAN paper, but no passage naming CTGAN, SDV, or any related component appears anywhere in the retrieved full text, so the citation could not be located or verified in context.
paper-synthesis-testing-black-box-2022.needs: The full text provided does not show the actual CTGAN citation or context; it may be in a reference list section not captured, or the OpenAlex citation link may be a mismatch. Cannot confirm how or whether CTGAN is engaged with in the body text.

paper-hpc-storage-service-autotuning-202.summary: This paper proposes VAE-ABO, a variational-autoencoder-guided asynchronous Bayesian optimization method for autotuning HPC storage service parameters, using transfer learning from prior tuning runs to warm-start a surrogate model, and demonstrates over 40x search speedup on a high-energy-physics workflow on Argonne's Theta supercomputer. Within their algorithm, a tabular VAE (TVAE) is fit on high-performing prior configurations and used to sample initialization points for the Bayesian optimizer, with the encoder/decoder/loss architecture described in the authors' own prose following the design in the CTGAN paper. TVAE, the tabular variational autoencoder introduced alongside CTGAN, is the model whose architecture is adopted and re-described to drive the surrogate initialization of their own optimization method.
paper-hpc-storage-service-autotuning-202.needs: Unclear whether the authors actually ran the CTGAN/SDV package's TVAE implementation ('available as an open source package') or reimplemented the architecture themselves from the description; the detailed encoder/decoder/loss walkthrough suggests a reimplementation (port) but the phrase about an open-source package leaves room for api_user.

paper-learning-behave-improving-covert-2.summary: This paper proposes Raven, a censorship-resistant email-based messaging system built around two behavior-based design principles: isolating covert channel operation from cover protocol operation, and modeling cover traffic on genuine human usage patterns. Raven trains a generative model on real user email logs to control the timing and sizes of transmitted messages, and its evaluation shows large improvements in false-positive rates for censors trying to detect the covert channel compared to a prior system (Mailet). The generative model is explicitly the CopulaGAN model from the Synthetic Data Vault project (referred to throughout as CTGAN), run directly via SDV's implementation to synthesize the email transmission-pattern data that underlies Raven's entire behavioral-realism evaluation.

paper-privacy-preserving-generative-adve.summary: This paper proposes pGAN, a privacy-preserving GAN architecture for generating synthetic Electronic Health Records that balances distribution fidelity, privacy, and utility, evaluated on classification and regression healthcare datasets using Nearest Neighbour Adversarial Accuracy and downstream ML performance. The authors benchmark their model against two other synthesizers trained on the same 80% training split. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni, 2018) is trained as one of two benchmark models compared against the proposed pGAN on privacy and utility metrics.
paper-privacy-preserving-generative-adve.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev TGAN package was run directly or a reimplementation was used.

paper-property-inference-attacks-against.summary: This paper introduces the first training-dataset property inference attack against GANs, inferring macro-level attributes (e.g., proportion of a sensitive attribute) of a target GAN's training set under both full and partial black-box settings, and shows the attack also boosts membership inference. Experiments are run over four representative GAN architectures across five property-inference tasks. TGAN, the tabular GAN from the Xu & Veeramachaneni line, is reimplemented by the authors from its published settings (LSTM sizes, batch size, Adam parameters) as one of the four target generative models attacked, using its mode-specific normalization for numeric variables.
paper-property-inference-attacks-against.needs: Unclear whether the sdv-dev TGAN codebase was ever invoked or the model was purely reimplemented from the paper's description; treated as a port given explicit architecture-level reconstruction.

paper-simulation-telemetry-signals-car-2.summary: This paper investigates using machine learning and deep learning techniques, including GANs, to synthetically generate automotive telemetry sensor data to reduce the cost and time of field data collection for predictive maintenance and anomaly-detection use cases. The abstract discusses the general landscape of synthetic data generation methods without detailing a specific model or pipeline. It cites the original Synthetic Data Vault paper as part of the background literature on synthetic data generation, without indicating that SDV software was run.
paper-simulation-telemetry-signals-car-2.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV software/library was actually run or merely cited in the background/related work section.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-ge.summary: This paper investigates GAN-based generation of synthetic telecommunication data for Wi-Fi signal quality, developing and comparing a Vanilla GAN and a Wasserstein GAN to produce features usable by specialized network-monitoring companies lacking real data. The authors select WGAN as their final model based on its ability to reproduce feature distributions and associations of the real data. In their related-work discussion, TGAN is mentioned only as a similar prior approach that evaluated its generative process on actual medical records, without being run or compared experimentally.

paper-metgan-memory-efficient-tabular-20.summary: This paper proposes MeTGAN, a memory-efficient redesign of CTGAN that replaces the dense conditional-vector layers and first-layer residual connection with sparse linear layers, cutting GPU memory usage by roughly 80% on high-cardinality categorical data while matching CTGAN's performance on ML efficacy, distribution similarity, and privacy metrics across Adult, News, and Loan datasets. The work directly modifies CTGAN's own generator/discriminator architecture and conditional vector to produce this new named variant.
paper-metgan-memory-efficient-tabular-20.needs: The OpenAlex metadata lists the cited SDV paper as the 2016 SDV DSAA paper, but the actual technical engagement in the full text is entirely with CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019), suggesting a citation-key mismatch rather than genuine SDV (Patki et al.) engagement.

paper-oct-gan-neural-ode-2021.summary: This paper proposes OCT-GAN, a conditional tabular GAN whose generator and discriminator are built from neural ordinary differential equations (NODEs), improving on prior tabular synthesizers by performing trajectory-based discrimination and ODE-transformed latent generation. It is evaluated on 13 datasets against multiple synthetic-data baselines including a Bayesian-network-style model, MedGAN, VEEGAN, TableGAN, and models the authors label 'TGAN' and 'TVAE' (both from the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper) across likelihood, classification, regression, and clustering tasks, and separately cites SDV's Gaussian-copula recursive table modeling as related prior work. CTGAN and TVAE (mislabeled 'TGAN'/'TVAE' in text) are run extensively as comparison baselines throughout the empirical evaluation, while the SDV Gaussian-copula relational approach is only cited as background.
paper-oct-gan-neural-ode-2021.needs: The text consistently calls the OpenAlex-matched CTGAN citation 'TGAN,' so it is unclear whether the authors ran the actual sdv-dev CTGAN package or their own reimplementation of the model described in the CTGAN paper; treated here as baseline_only per the paper's own framing as a compared baseline model.

paper-synthesizing-individual-consumers-.summary: This paper proposes a custom GAN-based approach to generate synthetic individual consumer credit histories for financial institutions, aiming to preserve statistical utility while protecting privacy, and evaluates the synthetic data's utility for educational/ML training purposes on real-world credit data. The authors build their own GAN model rather than using an existing package, describing prior tabular-data GAN work (TGAN) and the conditional-variable extension associated with CTGAN as background. TGAN and CTGAN are cited only as prior art describing tabular/conditional GAN architectures, with no SDV-family code run in the study.
paper-synthesizing-individual-consumers-.needs: None beyond confirming citation-only status; TGAN and CTGAN are described as prior tabular-GAN work but not executed.

preprint-demonstration-sqlyzr-platform-f.summary: This paper demonstrates SQLyzr, an interactive benchmark and evaluation platform for text-to-SQL models that supports fine-grained query classification, error analysis, workload alignment, and database scaling. As an optional preprocessing step for evaluating models under large-scale conditions, SQLyzr uses SDV to train a generative model on each database and synthesize additional rows preserving the original statistical properties. SDV's synthetic data generation framework is run as one of several preprocessing components of the platform to scale databases for evaluation.
preprint-demonstration-sqlyzr-platform-f.needs: No specific SDV synthesizer or algorithm (e.g., GaussianCopula, CTGAN) is named, so sdv_concept is left empty; SDV is used generically as a data-scaling tool.

preprint-evaluating-quality-synthetic-ge.summary: This paper benchmarks seven tabular synthetic data generators (including TVAE, CTGAN, PGM, PrivSyn, TabDDPM, TableDiffusion, and GReaT) across four datasets of varying scale, with systematic hyperparameter optimization for each model-dataset pair. It proposes a methodology for visualizing and quantifying fidelity of synthesized joint distributions and applies it to a domain-specific German Cancer Registries epidemiological dataset, revealing challenges in medical-domain adherence. CTGAN and TVAE are run directly as two of the seven benchmarked synthesizers, with their published hyperparameter ranges (embedding_dim, l2scale, loss_factor, compress_dims, decompress_dims) matching the CTGAN/TVAE implementation from the sdv-dev ecosystem, evaluated as subjects rather than as the paper's own method.

preprint-psygentab-privacy-preserving-fr.summary: PSyGenTAB is a privacy-preserving synthetic clinical tabular data generation framework that casts privacy-utility balancing as a constrained optimization problem solved via the Augmented Lagrangian Method, applied on top of generators such as REaLTabFormer and CTAB-GAN+ across multiple clinical benchmark datasets. The paper's related-work section credits TGAN with mode-specific normalization and autoregressive modeling and CTGAN with improved handling of imbalanced categorical attributes, but neither is run as a generator in the experiments. SDMetrics, however, is actually invoked (v0.12.0) as one of the framework's evaluation pipelines to compute an open-source structural Quality Score (KS Test, TVD) compared against a commercial MostlyAI accuracy score across all datasets.
preprint-psygentab-privacy-preserving-fr.needs: CTGAN and TGAN citations are related-work-only (citation_only); the load-bearing SDV usage is SDMetrics as an evaluation library, which drove the api_user/importance-3 call rather than the cited generator papers.

preprint-quantum-enhanced-synthetic-gene.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical framework using a Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) to generate synthetic minority-class samples for imbalanced tabular datasets (Iris and Telco Customer Churn), trained via KL-divergence minimization with parameter-shift optimization, and compares it against classical oversampling methods like SMOTE and its variants. CTGAN and TGAN are cited in the related-work section as prior conditional-GAN-based deep generative approaches for tabular data, but neither is implemented or run in the experiments. SDV's CTGAN and TGAN are mentioned only as related prior art in the paper's literature review.

preprint-tabscm-practical-framework-gene.summary: TabSCM is a mixed-type tabular data generator that preserves causal structure by orienting a CPDAG into a DAG, fitting root-node marginals, and learning topologically ordered structural assignments via conditional diffusion models and gradient-boosted trees, enabling counterfactual queries and fairness auditing. It is evaluated against GAN, diffusion, and LLM baselines on seven public datasets for statistical fidelity, downstream utility, and privacy. CTGAN is run as one of several baseline generators using its default parameter set, and SDMetrics' statistical-similarity and classifier-two-sample-test methodology is used to evaluate all generators including TabSCM.

paper-tailbooster-extreme-values-2026.summary: Addresses two failures at once for rare events in air transportation: generative models under-represent distributional tails, and they emit records that are individually plausible but operationally impossible, such as a short air time on a long route. A statistical layer extracts extremes by interquartile range to supply tail-focused training signal, and a learned anomaly-detection layer filters infeasible output afterwards. TVAE is the generative stage the framework is built around, and SDV's FixedCombinations constraint was tried for origin-destination consistency and rejected after it collapsed the distribution, replaced by the post-generation validity filter.

preprint-beyond-one-size-fits-2025.summary: This paper proposes MargNet, a neural-network-based differentially private tabular data synthesizer that incorporates adaptive marginal selection (as used in statistical methods like AIM) into neural network training, aiming to outperform both statistical and neural DP synthesis baselines on densely correlated datasets. The empirical comparisons center on DP-CTGAN, a differentially private descendant of CTGAN, evaluated as one of several baseline generators. The original SDV/CTGAN paper is cited only in passing as an example of a 'strong generative model' underlying gradient-DP methods, without its architecture or code being used directly.
preprint-beyond-one-size-fits-2025.needs: The citation to the SDV CTGAN paper is generic and not tied to any run algorithm; the paper's extensive DP-CTGAN baseline is a separate descendant work, not SDV's CTGAN itself, so importance/integration here reflect only the passing citation.

paper-cardiac-pci-synthetic-2025.summary: Compares five synthetic oversamplers on a registry of patients after percutaneous coronary intervention, measuring not only discrimination but calibration and confidence for each of six downstream classifiers, and finds that oversampling changes model behaviour rather than merely improving scores: recall rises at the cost of accuracy and calibration, and several generators are actively harmful. Three of the five oversamplers are SDV synthesizers, CTGAN, TVAE and GaussianCopula, each trained on the minority class and reported as its own block of results.

preprint-exploring-heterogeneity-tabular.summary: This paper proposes DATE, a diversity-aware tabular data generation framework that partitions heterogeneous tabular data into distributionally distinct subsets and uses LLMs with decision-tree-reasoning feedback and a multi-armed-bandit sampling algorithm to balance diversity and quality of generated data. It is evaluated against GAN-based and LLM-based baselines on classification and regression benchmarks, showing large error-rate reductions. CTGAN is run as the representative GAN-based baseline, with its results reported in the comparison tables against DATE.

paper-fcegan-counterfactual-2025.summary: Introduces counterfactual templates that let a user name which features may change at inference time rather than fixing the mutable set when the explainer is trained, and implements them in a generative adversarial explainer that also works black-box by learning from a historical prediction dataset instead of the classifier's internals, improving counterfactual validity over optimization-based benchmarks on economic and healthcare tables. CTGAN is the foundation the model is built on: its generator and discriminator architectures serve as FCEGAN's, its training-by-sampling supplies the real counterfactuals used in the discriminator loss, and an independently trained CTGAN discriminator is the paper's fakeness metric.

preprint-medequalizer-framework-investig.summary: This paper studies demographic representativeness bias in synthetic healthcare data generated from MIMIC-III using three GAN-based tabular synthesizers (MedGAN, HealthGAN, CTGAN), measuring subgroup imbalance with a logarithmic disparity metric. It introduces MedEqualizer, a model-agnostic augmentation framework that enriches underrepresented demographic subgroups before synthetic generation to improve fairness across all three generators. CTGAN is run as one of the three evaluated generative models, using its conditional generator to sample minority subgroups, with its mode-specific normalization and conditional training-by-sampling architecture described in detail.
preprint-medequalizer-framework-investig.needs: Reference [23], cited in-text as the source for MedGAN, is actually Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018 (TGAN), while the true CTGAN paper (Xu et al. 2019) is reference [22] -- likely a mis-citation by the authors. It is unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev/ctgan package or a custom reimplementation, since no library name or constructor parameters are given.

preprint-rebalancing-scales-systematic-m.summary: This is a systematic mapping study that screens 3041 papers down to 100 key studies on GAN-based oversampling for imbalanced data across domains such as healthcare, finance, and cybersecurity, producing categorizations of application domains, GAN techniques, and GAN variants. It surveys dozens of reviewed works that employ conditional tabular GAN (CTGAN) and its derivatives (e.g., K-Means CTGAN, CTAB-GAN) for minority-class oversampling, and separately lists Copula-GAN among the catalogued GAN variants. CTGAN and Copula-GAN, both part of the SDV ecosystem, are discussed only as items in the reviewed literature rather than run by the authors themselves.

preprint-synth-mia-testbed-auditing-2025.summary: This paper introduces Synth-MIA, an open-source Python library implementing 13 membership-inference-attack methods through a scikit-learn-like API, designed to unify and standardize empirical privacy auditing of tabular synthetic data generators. Using this testbed, the authors run the largest tabular synthesis privacy benchmark to date across multiple generator architectures and datasets, showing that higher synthetic data quality correlates with greater privacy leakage and that similarity-based privacy metrics correlate weakly with MIA results. CTGAN and TVAE, both originating from the CTGAN paper, are among the eight generative model architectures evaluated as privacy-leakage subjects, but were implemented via the Synthcity framework rather than SDV's own package.
preprint-synth-mia-testbed-auditing-2025.needs: CTGAN/TVAE were run via the Synthcity framework's implementations rather than the sdv-dev ctgan package directly, so the exact provenance of the code executed is a third-party wrapper, not confirmed SDV source.

preprint-digital-twin-strategy-examine-2.summary: This preprint introduces RCT-Twin-GAN, a statistically informed conditional GAN that generates a 'digital twin' of a randomized clinical trial conditioned on the covariate distribution of a second population, applied to reconcile discordant treatment effects between the SPRINT and ACCORD blood-pressure trials. The authors validate that their synthetic digital twins contain no duplicated rows from the original data using an evaluation approach they attribute to the Synthetic Data Vault paper. SDV is cited only as the source of this row-novelty evaluation concept, not as a generator or library actually run in the pipeline.
preprint-digital-twin-strategy-examine-2.needs: Unclear whether SDV/sdmetrics software was actually run for the novelty check or whether the authors merely cite the evaluation concept and reimplement it themselves.

paper-dp-2stage-2024.summary: Diagnoses why fine-tuning a language model for tabular synthesis under differential privacy degrades so sharply - the privacy budget is spent learning the table's serialization format rather than its content - and proposes a two-stage remedy that first learns the format non-privately from a pseudo dataset drawn from an out-of-distribution public table, then fits the sensitive data under DP-SGD with the format tokens masked out of the loss, holding fidelity better than GAN and VAE mechanisms at equal budget. CTGAN and TVAE are run from the Synthetic Data Vault project's own implementation as the non-private comparison arms, the paper's VAE and DP-VAE arms are adaptations of TVAE that swap mode-specific normalization for plain standardization, and CTGAN's mode-specific normalization is named in the introduction as an example of a preprocessing step that must itself satisfy differential privacy.

preprint-watermarking-generative-categor.summary: This paper proposes a statistical framework for watermarking generative categorical data, embedding secret signals at the distribution level by splitting and deterministically modifying one component of the data distribution, and verifying watermarks via an insertion inverse algorithm and total variation distance test. It targets synthetic tabular/categorical data generation broadly, motivated by concerns about provenance and copyright in AI-generated data. CTGAN is cited only in passing, in a list of tabular generative models (alongside TabDDPM and TabSyn) that motivate the need for watermarking, without being run or evaluated in the work.

preprint-netdiffus-network-traffic-gener.summary: This paper proposes NetDiffus, a framework that converts one-dimensional network traffic time-series into two-dimensional Gramian Angular Summation Field images and applies diffusion models to synthesize new representative images, improving fidelity and downstream ML task performance over prior GAN-based traffic generators. It evaluates the approach on seven network traffic traces for tasks like fingerprinting, anomaly detection, and classification. CTGAN is cited in the related-work discussion as one of several generative-model solutions for network traffic generation, but it is not run or benchmarked in the experiments.

preprint-one-step-gibbs-sampling-2023.summary: This preprint proposes a one-step Gibbs sampling method for generating synthetic household populations, likely for use in demographic or transportation demand modeling. No abstract or full text was available, so the scope of the method and its evaluation cannot be described further. The work cites the TGAN paper, apparently as related work on synthetic data generation, without evidence that TGAN was run or extended.
preprint-one-step-gibbs-sampling-2023.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN is merely cited or actually used/compared. Industry/use_case inferred loosely from title only (synthetic household generation).

preprint-learning-control-perspective-mi.summary: This preprint develops a control-theoretic framework for microfinance lending decisions that jointly targets financial inclusion, fairness, social welfare, and sustainability, accounting for group liability and insufficient credit history in developing regions. The authors validate their learning-and-control algorithm on real and synthetic datasets derived from the Kiva microloan dataset. The Synthetic Data Vault library is run directly via its sdv.lite TabularPreset FAST_ML preset to generate a large pool of synthetic loan applications used to augment the pre-processed Kiva data for experiments.

preprint-unified-framework-quantifying-p.summary: This paper introduces Anonymeter, an open-source statistical framework that quantifies singling-out, linkability, and inference privacy risks in synthetic tabular data, aligning the evaluation with GDPR's three anonymization criteria. The authors validate the framework through attack-based experiments on synthetic datasets with deliberately inserted leakages and on data generated with and without differential privacy, comparing against prior privacy-evaluation frameworks. CTGAN, run via the original sdv-dev/SDV implementation, is the primary generator used to produce the synthetic datasets (Adults, Texas, US Census) that the entire empirical evaluation of privacy risk is built on, alongside a DP variant (DPCTGAN).

preprint-machine-learning-models-evaluat.summary: This preprint evaluates several machine learning classifiers (Random Forest, Decision Tree, KNN, SVM, XGBoost) for predicting non-performing loans on a private Ethiopian bank's dataset, comparing class-imbalance treatments and identifying the most predictive features. CTGAN is used alongside KMeans-SMOTE as an over-sampling technique to address minority-class imbalance, with model performance evaluated separately on each; the KMeans-SMOTE over-sampled data ultimately yields better results than the CTGAN over-sampled data. CTGAN is run as one of two comparison over-sampling baselines and is outperformed by KMeans-SMOTE in the paper's headline result.

preprint-credit-scoring-model-imbalanced.summary: This preprint proposes a hybrid ensemble credit-scoring model, CNN-ATCN, that combines CNN for static financial feature extraction with an attention-augmented TCN for temporal dependencies, feeding a stacking classifier (LR, XGBoost, Adaboost, Random Forest) to predict loan default. To address the severe class imbalance typical of credit datasets, the authors use CTGAN to synthesize additional default-class transactions before training, and show on two real-world datasets that the augmented data improves accuracy, AUC, F1 and recall. CTGAN, described with its mode-specific normalization and conditional generator/training-by-sampling design, is run as the data-augmentation generator underpinning the whole experimental pipeline.
preprint-credit-scoring-model-imbalanced.needs: Not explicit whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was run or a custom reimplementation; no import/package name or constructor parameters given, only the algorithm's design description.

preprint-synthetic-observational-health-.summary: This is a broad literature review surveying published GAN-based approaches for generating synthetic observational health data (EHR-derived tabular, time-series, and multi-table data), cataloguing algorithms, their architectural adaptations, and evaluation metrics, and diagnosing why adoption in medical research had been slow. It discusses issues of benchmarking, data modelling, privacy, and reproducibility across the surveyed works rather than proposing a new generator itself. The Synthetic Data Vault is discussed as one of the few publications handling multi-relational tables based on Gaussian Copulas, and CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional design are described in detail as prior art that inspired several other reviewed algorithms (e.g. HealthGAN's data transformation adapted from SDV) but neither library is run by the authors.

paper-tgan-2018.summary: The first tabular GAN from the group, using an LSTM to generate columns sequentially for mixed discrete and continuous tables. Direct predecessor of CTGAN.

repo-sas-viya-machine-learning.summary: Code examples for machine-learning techniques on the SAS Viya platform. A credit-card GAN example imports `CTGANSynthesizer` as the tabular generator. It records a commercial analytics vendor teaching CTGAN alongside its own tooling.
